
```yaml
claim_id: claim_laws_0012

claim_kind: thesis

greek_terms:
  - ἥττων ἡ πόλις αὑτῆς
  - κρείττων τε καὶ ἀγαθή
```


```yaml
claim_id: claim_laws_0014

content: A judge who, receiving one kinship group in discord, destroys none of them but reconciles them and establishes laws for them so that they can remain friends for the remaining time is far better than a judge who destroys the bad and commands the better to rule themselves, or one who makes the good rule and lets the worse live in willing subjection.
greek_terms:
  - διαλλάξας
  - νόμους αὐτοῖς θείς
  - ὥστε εἶναι φίλους

  - kind: posed_for_examination

final_status: left_standing

The record does not establish that this thesis has been tested against counter-examples; it functions as a normative premise for the subsequent argument about the lawgiver's orientation toward internal peace rather than external war.
review_status: accepted
```

```yaml
speaker: ΑΘ.
claim_kind: thesis
content: A city's victory over itself is not among the best things but among the necessary things; similarly, someone who attends only to external warfare and treats it as primary would never become a correct statesman or an accurate lawgiver. The lawgiver should legislate the things of war for the sake of peace rather than the things of peace for the sake of war.
greek_terms:

final_status: left_standing

Cleinias concedes the argument seems correctly stated but expresses surprise that Cretan and Spartan customs appear to have been crafted entirely for the sake of war (628e). The record does not establish that Cleinias retracts his surprise or that the thesis has been reconciled with Spartan practice.
review_status: accepted
```

```yaml
content: "Good things are twofold: human goods and divine goods. The human goods depend on the divine ones, and if a city receives the greater goods it also acquires the lesser, but if not, it is deprived of both. The lesser goods are led by health, second is beauty, third is strength for running and all other bodily movements, fourth is wealth — not blind but sharp-sighted, if it follows wisdom. The first of the divine goods is wisdom, second is a moderate disposition of soul with intelligence, third is justice mixed with courage, fourth is courage."
```



```yaml
claim_id: claim_laws_0423

speaker: ΑΘ.
claim_kind: method_rule
content: "Once time has passed and the constitution endures, the selection of magistrates shall be as follows: all who bear hoplite or cavalry arms and have shared in war in their own age-groups shall share in the election; the election shall be held in whatever temple the city holds most honored; each man shall bring to the god's altar a tablet inscribed with the candidate's name with patronymic, tribe, and deme, and also his own name likewise; anyone who wishes may remove any tablet that appears not to his liking and place it in the agora for no less than thirty days; the magistrates shall display the tablets judged first up to three hundred for the whole city to see; the city shall similarly vote again from these; the second-round selectees, one hundred, shall be displayed again to all; the third round shall be by vote from the hundred, each man proceeding through sacrificial victims; and the thirty-seven who receive the most votes shall be declared magistrates."
greek_terms:
  []
stance_events:
  - kind: asserted
    stephanus_span: 753b-753d

final_status: left_standing
observation_ids:

limits: This is a procedural rule for future magistrate selections after the initial founding period. It is explicitly conditional on the passage of time and the endurance of the constitution. It does not address how the initial thirty-seven law-guardians will govern or how other magistracies will be filled.
review_status: accepted
```

```yaml
content: Election of the preliminary candidates for examiners proceeds by each citizen nominating up to three men (at least fifty years old) whom he judges best in every way except himself; the top half by vote count advance, with ties broken by youth, and the process repeats until three unequal winners remain; final ties are settled by lot.
```
